submission.name: Market Minute
submission.tagline: Swipe through money explainers, then see how a simple investing rule reacts to market signals.
submission.inspiration: Short financial videos are easy to find, but it can be hard to tell whether a clip explains a useful idea or just makes a bold claim. We wanted to connect bite-sized learning with a small, transparent way to explore how market signals can inform a rule.
submission.what_it_does: The web prototype shows short finance explainers and lets users mark clips as useful, then presents a paper-trading sandbox with a few adjustable rules and sample sentiment signals. A rough content check uses sentence similarity to flag clips that appear off topic, and an ElevenLabs voice can read a clip summary aloud.
submission.how_we_built_it: The React and TypeScript interface has separate feed and sandbox views, while a FastAPI backend provides placeholder clip records and rule inputs. We prototyped sentence-transformer checks in Python and a market-signal calculation inspired by a trading-rule project, but those pieces are not wired into the feed or each other. The BNY angle is the financial education and decision-support workflow, and voice narration is an optional accessibility feature.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: The demo is not connected end-to-end: the feed, similarity check, paper-trading calculation, and voice playback work only as separate pieces or mocked screens. We did not complete user accounts, real market data, or a rewards system, so the displayed signals should not be treated as investment advice.
submission.accomplishments: We built a navigable feed mockup and separate working prototypes for content similarity and a simple rule calculation. We are proud that the sandbox makes its inputs visible instead of presenting a mysterious prediction.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned that financial content review is more nuanced than matching a clip to a topic label, and that market rules need clear assumptions. AI tools helped us sketch summaries and interface copy, but we still need human review before trusting generated explanations.
submission.whats_next: We would connect clip transcripts to the review service, add sourced market data for paper trading, and make the voice playback part of the clip view. A later version could include progress tracking and verified educational material without tying learning rewards to speculative token mechanics.
